newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Lee seeks cabinet reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Lee seeks cabinet reshuffle.

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui has asked Premier Lien Chan to reshuffle his cabinet next week in an effort to appease growing public outcry over the island's worsening social disorder, a senior official said on Wednesday.
Lee, however, declined to accept Lien's resignation offer.

"I have retained Premier Lien Chan...I have asked Lien Chan to make some adjustments in the cabinet," Wu Poh-hsiung, ruling Nationalist Party secretary-general, quoted Lee as saying at the party's central standing committee meeting.

Wu said Lien had tendered his resignation on Sunday to take responsibility for the government's failure to check a spate of violent crimes, the latest of which was the gruesome murder of a popular actress's teenage daughter in April.
Wu said Lien was expected to deliver a list of reshuffled cabinet positions for approval during next Wednesday's central standing committee meeting.
Taiwanese have been outraged and grief-stricken since police found the body of 17-year-old Pai Hsiao-yen, daughter of actress Pai Ping-ping, floating naked in a river last week.
Her kidnappers have not been caught.
"The top priority is to resolve the case," Wu quoted Lee as saying.
More than 50,000 people demonstrated on Sunday to demand the resignation of Lien and a cabinet reshuffle.
About 40 students rallied in front of the cabinet building on Monday to protest against Taiwan's deteriorating social order and ask Lien to take responsibility.

Lee, who last week apologised for what he called "worsening social law and order", planned to meet leaders of private groups on Friday and convene a national conference to discuss the island's mounting crime problems.

State television speculated that Interior Minister Lin Feng-cheng, under fire for the recent flurry of violent crimes, would be replaced by former Justice Minister Ma Ying-jeou, currently a minister without portfolio.
It added that government spokesman Su Chi would be replaced by vice foreign minister Chen Chien-jen.
Council of Agriculture Chairman Tjiu Mau-ying would also step down, the television reported, but it did not name Tjiu's replacement.
Some government agricultural departments have been criticised for failing to prevent a hog epidemic that forced Taiwan to halt all pork exports.
Meanwhile, a newspaper poll released on Tuesday showed Lien's approval rating had sunk to a new low.
Only 24 percent of 762 people interviewed by the United Daily News on Monday said they were satisfied with Lien's performance, down six percentage points from a similar poll a week ago.
